collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder who has never married and a child aged 5-12)

collection.description: A child asks an elder who never married if they were ever sad about it: answer honestly, or ask why they want to know.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) never married and never wanted to. (subject.He/she) has had a full, busy life: friends, work, a garden that's the envy of the village, and more of the village's children underfoot than (subject.he/she) can count. Today (friend), one of them, asks very seriously, "Were you sad you didn't get married?"

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) thinks about it, because it's a fair question. "No," (subject.he/she) says. "Sometimes I've been lonely. Everyone is, married or not. But I've never been sad about that." (friend) nods slowly. "I might not get married," (friend.he/she) says. "That's allowed," says (subject). "You might. You might not. You'll find out." (friend) seems satisfied, and goes off to dig a hole.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) asks why (friend) wants to know. (friend) shrugs. "Someone said grown-ups who don't get married are sad." (subject) laughs, a big real laugh. "Do I look sad?" (friend) looks. (subject) has mud on (subject.his/her) nose and a flower behind (subject.his/her) ear and is holding a giant squash. "No," says (friend). "Well, then," says (subject).
